2016: English record producer, arranger, composer, conductor, audio engineer and musician, Sir George Martin died aged 90. He worked as EMI records in-house record producer and became known as the so-called fifth Beatle. Martin produced all but one of The Beatles albums giving him 30 No.1 hit singles in the UK and 23 No.1 hits in the US. He also produced many other acts including: Matt Monro, Cilla Black, Gerry & The Pacemakers, Billy J. He was a founding member and keyboard player with the Grateful Dead and played in the group from 1965 to 1972. Daily Devotional

March 8

5 This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all. 6 If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth: 7 But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. (1 John 1:5-7 KJV)

The term light in the bible is referring to that which is good and holy, whereas darkness is referring to that which is evil or unholy. It is saying that God is completely holy with nothing bad (no darkness) in Him. If we say we are walking with God, and yet our lives are full of darkness (sin), then we are not telling the truth, as our lives will reflect just who we are walking with, God or Satan (Romans 6:16). You judge a tree by it’s fruit, and a person by their actions.

All born again believers are in God (light), but do not necessarily walk in the light. Whether you walk after God or after this world (Satan), is reflected by your actions. It is not meant for man to guide his own footsteps (Jeremiah 10:23), so letting God guide us is how we are supposed to live. If we walk after God, it doesn’t mean we don’t fall short and sin, as we all sin (1 John 1:8), but it does mean that we are trying to live a holy life as best we can (1 Peter 1:15). When we walk in the light the blood of Jesus will cleanse us of all our sins. Christians who walk in the dark (sin) stand the chance of hardening their hearts toward God, and eventually can become reprobate, and lose their salvation (Revelation 3:5), so walk in the light all your life. Thank you Jesus!
